summary: New Zealand beat Ireland 28-24 in a Rugby World Cup quarter-final at the Stade de France, extending Ireland's record of failing to win a knockout match. Ireland's final 37-phase attack, lasting five minutes, ended in a turnover deep in the New Zealand 22. The match swung back and forth, and the All Blacks now face Argentina in the semi-final.
one_line: New Zealand edged Ireland 28-24 in a thrilling World Cup quarter-final, ending Ireland's 37-phase final attack and extending their knockout curse.
key_facts: New Zealand beat Ireland 28-24 in the Rugby World Cup quarter-final at the Stade de France in Paris.
It was the eighth time in 10 Rugby World Cups that Ireland went out in the quarter-finals, and they have never won a knockout match.
Ireland's last attack began with 77 minutes on the clock and lasted 37 phases over about five minutes before a turnover deep in the New Zealand 22.
Ireland haven't led a World Cup quarter-final since the first half of the 1995 defeat to France, 10,353 days earlier.
New Zealand led 13-0 early; no team had ever squandered a lead that large in a World Cup quarter-final.
Leicester Fainga'anuku scored New Zealand's first try; he started only because Mark Telea breached team protocol earlier in the week.
Bundee Aki scored for Ireland on 27 minutes and had a tournament-high 61 carries, 33 dominant carries and 23 defenders beaten before the weekend.
Jamison Gibson-Park scored from a lineout maul just before half-time to cut the score to 18-17 while Aaron Smith was in the sin-bin.
Will Jordan scored after Richie Mo'unga's dummy, and Ardie Savea also scored a try for New Zealand.
A penalty try made it 25-24 with 17 minutes left and sent Codie Taylor to the sin-bin; Jordie Barrett's penalty made it 28-24.
Ireland's players formed a figure of eight during the Haka in memory of Anthony Foley, who died in 2016.
Johnny Sexton played his final match before retirement; Ian Foster leaves as New Zealand coach after the tournament, to be replaced by Scott Robertson.
New Zealand face Argentina in the semi-final next Friday and could lift the Webb Ellis Cup for a fourth time.
